kill_fact: NONE. Attacked on stale-anchor, number-truth, thesis-weakness and hidden-disqualifier axes; no fact breaks the value case. Every load-bearing bear-side figure verifies against primary filings, several to the dollar: shares 397.5M (10-Q cover, 2026-06-11); net debt $1.44B is EXACT under the lease-inclusive convention (balance-sheet debt $6,645M = senior notes $6,151M + commercial paper $494M, plus operating-lease liabilities $420M, minus cash+ST investments $5,626M = $1,439M as of 2026-05-29; strict ex-lease convention would be ~$1.02B, i.e. the bear is conservative); FY25 segment anchors Digital Media $17.65B / Digital Experience $5.86B verify verbatim against the Q4 FY25 release. The Semrush-dressing claim -- the bear's centerpiece -- is confirmed by two primary guidance tables: the Dec-10-2025 FY26 target of 10.2% ending-ARR growth explicitly stated it 'does not include any contributions from Semrush,' while the Jun-11-2026 release re-affirms the identical 10.2% now 'factor[ing] in the acquisition of Semrush' with ~$480M of the $27.10B ARR acquired, i.e. an organic cut of ~1.9pts on the $25.66B entering base. CFO Durn departed 2026-06-15 (interim CFO Steve Day); CEO successor still unnamed as of 2026-07-02 (search announced 2026-03-12, Narayen stays Chair). At $210.98 live (52wk low $190.12), market cap $83.9B / EV ~$85B sits ~47% below even the bear's own adverse SoP EV (~$159B) and ~7.6x the FCF cross-check base ($10.5B TTM FCF: FY25 OCF $10.03B, H1 FY26 OCF $5.12B), so the cheapness is real on verified current numbers -- the open question is forward FCF erosion (value trap), which is a risk the bear correctly prices, not a falsifiable kill fact.
corrections: Three load-bearing corrections. (1) METHOD BREAK on the SoP floor: per 10-Q Note 15, Adobe combined Digital Media / Digital Experience / Publishing & Advertising into a SINGLE operating and reportable segment in Q1 FY26 -- the FY25 splits the bear SoP rests on ($17.65B/$5.86B/$0.26B) are the FINAL vintage of segment disclosure and can never be re-verified or tracked forward; the only forward lens is customer-group subscription revenue (Business Professionals & Consumers $1.85B/q +16%, Creative & Marketing Professionals $4.54B/q +13%). Treat the segment-free FCF cross-check (~$373/sh at 14x $10.6B) as the real bear floor, and note the governance tell: management removed the exact disclosure that would expose Digital Media deterioration, mid-pivot. (2) MISSED RESOLVED DISQUALIFIER: the DOJ/FTC ROSCA action (filed 2024-06-17, N.D. Cal.) settled 2026-03-12/13 for $150M ($75M cash + $75M free services) PLUS a permanent injunction mandating simple cancellation -- immaterial vs $10.5B FCF and it removes the litigation tail, but the injunction is a structural churn headwind on individual subscribers landing exactly where the freemium pivot cuts. Related: the Figma securities class action was dismissed in full (2025-03-27, leave to amend denied 2025-11-07, on appeal). (3) NEW CRACK the debate missed: a $70M non-cash goodwill impairment on the Publishing & Advertising reporting unit in Q2 FY26 ($0.17/sh GAAP) -- the first impairment print of the AI era, in the smallest unit. Minor: Semrush closed 2026-04-28 (10-Q Note 3, $1.87B primarily cash), not April 29. Supporting bear color verified: H1 FY26 buyback 16.6M shares/$4,588M (avg ~$276 -- management bought all the way down), $26.78B authorization remaining; FY26 non-GAAP EPS guide raised to $24.35-24.45 with ~399M diluted shares.
evidence: Adobe 10-Q, quarter ended 2026-05-29 (SEC EDGAR accession 0000796343-26-000112, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000796343/000079634326000112/adbe-20260529.htm): cover 397.5M shares o/s as of 2026-06-11; balance-sheet debt $1,843M current + $4,802M long-term, senior notes carrying $6,151M, commercial paper $494M @3.76%, operating-lease liabilities $420M, cash $4,919M + ST investments $707M; Note 15: single reportable segment effective Q1 FY26; Note 3: Semrush acquisition completed 2026-04-28 for $1.87B; DOJ ROSCA settlement agreed 2026-03-12, stipulation of dismissal filed 2026-03-13; $70M goodwill impairment (Publishing & Advertising); $26.78B repurchase authority remaining, H1 buyback 16.6M shares/$4,588M; H1 operating cash flow $5,123M.

Adobe Q2 FY2026 earnings press release, 2026-06-11 (8-K Ex-99.1, accession 0000796343-26-000109): record revenue $6.62B; total ARR $27.10B including ~$480M from Semrush; FY26 targets 'factor in the acquisition of Semrush' -- total ending ARR growth 10.2% YoY, revenue $26.50-26.60B, non-GAAP EPS raised to $24.35-24.45 (~399M diluted shares); GAAP EPS $4.25 incl. $0.17 goodwill-impairment charge; CFO Dan Durn departing 2026-06-15, Steve Day interim CFO.

Adobe Q4 FY2025 earnings press release, 2025-12-10 (Ex-99.1): FY26 targets 'do not include any contributions from Semrush Holdings, Inc.' with the SAME total ending ARR growth target of 10.2% YoY; entering-FY2026 total ARR $25.66B; FY25 Digital Media segment revenue $17.65B (+11%), Digital Experience $5.86B (+9%) -- the final segment-reported vintage anchoring both SoPs.

DOJ U.S. Attorney's Office N.D. Cal. press release, March 2026 (justice.gov/usao-ndca/pr/adobe-agrees-150-million-settlement-and-injunction-resolve-alleged-violations-restore): Adobe agrees to $150M settlement ($75M civil payment + $75M free services) and injunction requiring simple cancellation under ROSCA.
